packages.detail.noPaths: No path is listed for this package
packages.empty.body: Data that DSM packages keep here, such as Container Manager or Active Backup, appears once a scan finds it
packages.empty.title: No package data on this volume
packages.explain.iscsi_luns: Thin-provisioned LUNs return deleted space to the volume only when space reclamation is enabled and the initiator sends UNMAP; thick-provisioned LUNs have their configured capacity allocated up front. VMM images are managed in Virtual Machine Manager > Image, where their selected storage is shown
packages.explain.vmm_virtual_disks: Virtual Machine Manager stores virtual disks under @iSCSI/LUN/VDISK_*. Their storage is checked in Virtual Machine Manager > Virtual Machine, not inferred from the Btrfs path
packages.status.unconfirmed.hint: This data layout was not confirmed on this DSM version, so the figures are a best reading
packages.title: Packages
packages.intro: Most of this space is what the packages need to run, and usually can't be deleted directly. To free some, clean up in the package's own settings, or uninstall packages you no longer use
packages.scope: Package data kept in shared folders, such as Active Backup for Business or Hyper Backup backups and Surveillance Station recordings, is listed here too. Explore also counts it in that shared folder's size, so don't add the two together
packages.detail.never: Syno Reclaim never deletes package data

packages.detail.notRead.one: {count} snapshot inside this data was not read
packages.detail.notRead.other: {count} snapshots inside this data were not read

packages.detail.unknown: {size} of this data could not be traced to its files
packages.how.synology_drive: Open Synology Drive Admin Console > Team Folder, select a folder, choose Edit and lower how many versions it keeps
packages.how.synology_drive_sharesync: Open Synology Drive ShareSync and remove sync tasks you no longer need
packages.how.active_backup: Open Active Backup for Business and delete backup versions or tasks you no longer need, or shorten the retention policy. Never delete its files directly
packages.how.active_backup_microsoft_365: Open Active Backup for Microsoft 365 and delete backup versions or tasks you no longer need, or shorten the retention policy. Never delete its files directly
packages.how.active_backup_google_worksp: Open Active Backup for Google Workspace and delete backup versions or tasks you no longer need, or shorten the retention policy. Never delete its files directly
packages.how.container_manager: Open Container Manager: under Container, delete stopped containers you don't need; then under Image, delete images no container uses
packages.how.share_snapshots: Open Snapshot Replication > Snapshots and delete snapshots you no longer need. The Snapshots page here shows which ones free the most
packages.how.snapshot_replication: Open Snapshot Replication > Replication and remove replication tasks you no longer need
packages.how.surveillance_data: This is Surveillance Station's own data, such as its database. Manage it in Surveillance Station. Recordings are kept in the surveillance shared folder and count there
packages.how.iscsi_luns: Open SAN Manager > LUN and delete LUNs you no longer use
packages.how.vmm_virtual_disks: Open Virtual Machine Manager > Virtual Machine and delete virtual machines or virtual disks you no longer need
packages.how.cloud_sync: Open Cloud Sync and remove connections you no longer need
packages.how.usb_copy: Open USB Copy and delete tasks you no longer need
packages.how.hyper_backup_cache: Open Hyper Backup and edit or delete the backup task that uses this cache
packages.how.syno_reclaim: Open Scan history and choose Clear cache. Reports and job history are kept
packages.how.packages: These are the installed packages themselves. To free this space, uninstall packages you no longer use in Package Center
packages.how.package_files: Data the packages need to run. It is freed when you uninstall the package that uses it in Package Center
packages.how.databases: Databases DSM and packages need to run. Don't delete them; uninstalling a package in Package Center removes its database
packages.how.dsm_temp: Temporary files DSM clears by itself
packages.how.dsm_quota: Files DSM needs for user and shared folder quotas. Don't delete them; change quotas in Control Panel › User & Group or Shared Folder
packages.how.other_dsm_service_data: Data DSM or a package keeps at the root of the volume. Uninstalling the package that uses it in Package Center frees it
packages.own.clearable: Clearable cache: {size}. Reports and job history are kept
